items.title: Graded algebras, graded modules, and the graded tensor product
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A $\mathbb Z/2$-graded $k$-vector space is a direct sum $A=A^0\oplus A^1$; a homogeneous element $a\in A^i$ has parity $|a|=i\in\{0,1\}$. A $\mathbb Z/2$-graded unital associative $k$-algebra is such a space with $1\in A^0$ and $A^iA^j\subseteq A^{i+j\pmod 2}$. A graded left module is a module $M=M^0\oplus M^1$ satisfying $A^iM^j\subseteq M^{i+j\pmod 2}$. A graded submodule is an $A$-submodule $N=N^0\oplus N^1$; a graded-simple module is nonzero and has no proper nonzero graded submodule. An isomorphism of graded modules preserves both parity components.

For graded algebras $A,B$, their graded tensor product $A\widehat\otimes_k B$ has underlying vector space $A\otimes_kB$, parity $(A\widehat\otimes B)^r=\bigoplus_{i+j=r}A^i\otimes_kB^j$, and multiplication

$$
(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=(-1)^{|b||a'|}(aa'\otimes bb')
$$

for homogeneous factors, extended by the finite sum

$$
\sum_{i,j,r,s\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{jr}(a_i a'_r\otimes b_j b'_s),\qquad a=\sum_i a_i,\ b=\sum_j b_j,\ a'=\sum_r a'_r,\ b'=\sum_s b'_s.
$$

Each parity projection is linear, so this formula is $k$-multilinear in the four inputs and therefore defines a multiplication on $(A\otimes_kB)\times(A\otimes_kB)$ by [[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The unit is $1_A\otimes1_B$. For three homogeneous tensors, both associative bracketings contribute the sign exponent $|b||a'|+|b||a''|+|b'||a''|$, so the multiplication is associative.

items.title: Real, complex, and quaternion coefficient algebras and matrix notation
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb C=\mathbb R[x]/(x^2+1)$ be the complex field, whose elements have unique coordinates $z=a+b\mathrm i$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]], [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]). Write $\bar z=a-b\mathrm i$ for complex conjugation ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]). Let

$$
\mathbb H=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}:z,w\in\mathbb C\right\}\subseteq M_2(\mathbb C)
$$

with addition and multiplication inherited from matrices. This is a real associative algebra: multiplying the matrices with parameters $(z,w)$ and $(z',w')$ gives the matrix with parameters $(zz'-w\bar w',\,zw'+w\bar z')$. Its real basis is $1,i,j,k$, where
$i=\operatorname{diag}(\mathrm i,-\mathrm i)$, $j=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $k=ij$; these satisfy $i^2=j^2=k^2=-1$, $ij=k$, $jk=i$, $ki=j$, and reversing any of the last three products changes its sign.

For $D\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C,\mathbb H\}$ and a positive integer $m$, $M_m(D)$ is the associative algebra of $m\times m$ matrices with entries in $D$. The direct sum $A\oplus B$ of algebras has componentwise addition and multiplication. The opposite algebra $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ has the same addition and unit as $D$, with multiplication $d\cdot_{\mathrm{op}}e:=ed$. A left module is **simple** when it is nonzero and has no proper nonzero submodule ([[def-simple-module]]). For a simple left $M_m(D)$-module $S$, its coefficient type is $D$ when $\operatorname{End}_{M_m(D)}(S)\cong D^{\mathrm{op}}$; the classification theorem below proves the matrix-algebra cases used on this page.

items.title: The Clifford quotient has its canonical parity grading
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, let $B$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$ (possibly degenerate), and put $Q(v)=B(v,v)$. Form the plus-$Q$ Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)$ as in [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]]. Then the grading of the tensor algebra by tensor length modulo $2$ descends to a canonical $\mathbb Z/2$-grading

$$
\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)=\mathrm{Cl}^0(V,Q)\oplus\mathrm{Cl}^1(V,Q)
$$

in which $1\in\mathrm{Cl}^0(V,Q)$ and every canonical generator $\bar v$ lies in $\mathrm{Cl}^1(V,Q)$. Here a $\mathbb Z/2$-graded algebra and its even part are as in [[def-clifford-graded-algebra-module-and-tensor-product]]. No nondegeneracy assumption on $Q$ is needed.

items.title: The zero-dimensional Clifford algebra is the base field
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$, let $V=0$, and let $Q$ be the unique quadratic form on $V$. Then the plus-$Q$ Clifford algebra is $\mathrm{Cl}(0,Q)\cong k$ as a unital $k$-algebra.

items.title: Quaternion conjugation and division
items.statement:
For $h=a+bi+cj+dk\in\mathbb H$, define $\bar h=a-bi-cj-dk$ and $N(h)=a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2\in\mathbb R$. Quaternion conjugation is an involution and reverses products, $\overline{hg}=\bar g\bar h$. Moreover,

$$
h\bar h=\bar h h=N(h)1.
$$

In particular, every nonzero $h$ is invertible, with $h^{-1}=\bar h/N(h)$, so $\mathbb H$ is a real division algebra.

items.title: Graded modules over an algebra with an invertible odd element
items.statement: Let $A=A^0\oplus A^1$ be a $\mathbb Z/2$-graded unital associative algebra over a field, and suppose it contains an invertible homogeneous element $u\in A^1$. For left modules, the rule $M\mapsto M^0$ gives a bijection between isomorphism classes of graded-simple $A$-modules (with even isomorphisms) and isomorphism classes of simple $A^0$-modules. An inverse sends a left $A^0$-module $N$ to the induced graded module $A\otimes_{A^0}N$.

items.title: Tensor identities for the real division algebras
items.statement:
With $\mathbb H$, $M_m(D)$, and direct sums as in [[def-real-quaternion-matrix-algebra-notation]], the following are real-algebra isomorphisms:

$$\mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C,\qquad \mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H\cong M_2(\mathbb C),\qquad \mathbb H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H\cong M_4(\mathbb R).$$

and, for $D,E\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C,\mathbb H\}$ and positive integers $m,n$,

$$M_m(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}M_n(E)\cong M_{mn}(D\otimes_{\mathbb R}E).$$

items.title: Even subalgebras of real and complex Clifford algebras
items.statement:
Use the plus-square convention $v^2=Q(v)1$. For the real standard form $Q_{p,q}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p x_i^2-\sum_{j=1}^q x_{p+j}^2$, write $\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}^0$ for the even part of the canonical $\mathbb Z/2$ grading. If $p>0$, then

$$
\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}^0\cong \mathrm{Cl}_{q,p-1};
$$

if $p=0$ and $q>0$, then $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,q}^0\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{0,q-1}$. For the standard complex form $Q_n(z)=\sum_{i=1}^n z_i^2$ with $n>0$, the even subalgebra is isomorphic over $\mathbb C$ to $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n-1}(\mathbb C)$, the complex Clifford algebra on $n-1$ generators each having square $-1$, and hence to the standard complex Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_{n-1}(\mathbb C)$.

items.title: Low-dimensional real Clifford algebra models
items.statement:
Use the positive-square-first convention $Q_{p,q}=\sum_{i=1}^p x_i^2-\sum_{j=1}^q x_{p+j}^2$, and let $M_2(D)$ have the meaning in [[def-real-quaternion-matrix-algebra-notation]]. Then

| Signature | Algebra |
|---|---|
| $(1,0)$ | $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R$ |
| $(0,1)$ | $\mathbb C$ |
| $(2,0)$ | $M_2(\mathbb R)$ |
| $(1,1)$ | $M_2(\mathbb R)$ |
| $(0,2)$ | $\mathbb H$ |

items.title: The graded tensor product for orthogonal sums of quadratic spaces
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$, and let $(V,Q)$ and $(W,R)$ be finite-dimensional quadratic spaces over $k$, with associated symmetric bilinear forms $B_Q,B_R$ defined by $B_Q(v,v')=(Q(v+v')-Q(v)-Q(v'))/2$ and likewise for $R$. Give $V\oplus W$ the orthogonal-sum form $(Q\oplus R)(v,w)=Q(v)+R(w)$. With each Clifford generator odd in the canonical grading of [[lem-clifford-quotient-has-canonical-z2-grading]], the canonical map

$$\Phi:\mathrm{Cl}(V\oplus W,Q\oplus R)\longrightarrow\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)\widehat\otimes_k\mathrm{Cl}(W,R),\qquad (v,w)\longmapsto\bar v\otimes1+1\otimes\bar w$$

is an isomorphism of graded $k$-algebras. No nondegeneracy assumption is needed.

items.title: Real Clifford signature recurrences and eightfold periodicity
items.statement:
Let $\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ be the real algebra for the form with $p$ positive and $q$ negative squares, using $v^2=Q(v)1$. As ungraded real algebras, for $p,q,n\ge0$,

$$\mathrm{Cl}_{p+1,q+1}\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}\otimes_{\mathbb R}M_2(\mathbb R),\qquad \mathrm{Cl}_{n+2,0}\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}\otimes_{\mathbb R}M_2(\mathbb R),\qquad \mathrm{Cl}_{0,n+2}\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H.$$

The pure-signature algebras through dimension eight are

| $n$ | $\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}$ | $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}$ |
|---:|---|---|
| $0$ | $\mathbb R$ | $\mathbb R$ |
| $1$ | $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R$ | $\mathbb C$ |
| $2$ | $M_2(\mathbb R)$ | $\mathbb H$ |
| $3$ | $M_2(\mathbb C)$ | $\mathbb H\oplus\mathbb H$ |
| $4$ | $M_2(\mathbb H)$ | $M_2(\mathbb H)$ |
| $5$ | $M_2(\mathbb H)\oplus M_2(\mathbb H)$ | $M_4(\mathbb C)$ |
| $6$ | $M_4(\mathbb H)$ | $M_8(\mathbb R)$ |
| $7$ | $M_8(\mathbb C)$ | $M_8(\mathbb R)\oplus M_8(\mathbb R)$ |
| $8$ | $M_{16}(\mathbb R)$ | $M_{16}(\mathbb R)$ |

For every $n\ge0$, the pure algebras satisfy

$$\mathrm{Cl}_{n+8,0}\cong M_{16}(\mathrm{Cl}_{n,0}),\qquad \mathrm{Cl}_{0,n+8}\cong M_{16}(\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n}).$$

items.title: The ordinary tensor product does not model an orthogonal Clifford sum
items.statement: For all quadratic spaces, the ordinary algebra tensor product $\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathrm{Cl}(W,R)$, with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$, is the Clifford algebra of the orthogonal sum with its canonical factor maps.

items.title: Real and complex Clifford algebra classification with explicit signature
items.statement:
Let $n=p+q$, let $r$ be the residue of $p-q$ modulo $8$ in $\{0,1,\ldots,7\}$, and use $v^2=Q(v)1$ with signature ordered $(+^p,-^q)$. For every nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$, the real Clifford algebra is

| $r$ | parity of $n$ | $\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ |
|---:|:---:|---|
| $0$ | even | $M_{2^{n/2}}(\mathbb R)$ |
| $1$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\mathbb R)\oplus M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\mathbb R)$ |
| $2$ | even | $M_{2^{n/2}}(\mathbb R)$ |
| $3$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\mathbb C)$ |
| $4$ | even | $M_{2^{(n-2)/2}}(\mathbb H)$ |
| $5$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-3)/2}}(\mathbb H)\oplus M_{2^{(n-3)/2}}(\mathbb H)$ |
| $6$ | even | $M_{2^{(n-2)/2}}(\mathbb H)$ |
| $7$ | odd | $M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\mathbb C)$ |

Only signatures with $p,q\ge0$ are considered; in the feasible rows the displayed exponents are nonnegative. For a nondegenerate complex quadratic form on dimension $n$, its Clifford algebra is

$$\mathrm{Cl}_n(\mathbb C)\cong\begin{cases}M_{2^{n/2}}(\mathbb C),&n\text{ even},\\M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\mathbb C)\oplus M_{2^{(n-1)/2}}(\mathbb C),&n\text{ odd}.\end{cases}$$

These matrix-algebra classifications require nondegeneracy; no such classification is asserted for degenerate forms.

items.title: Irreducible graded Clifford modules and real, complex, and quaternionic types
items.statement:
Let $A=\mathrm{Cl}_{p,q}$ be a positive-dimensional standard real Clifford algebra with the canonical grading from [[lem-clifford-quotient-has-canonical-z2-grading]], and write $A^0$ for its even subalgebra. If $p>0$ then $A^0\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{q,p-1}$, and if $p=0$ then $A^0\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{0,q-1}$. For the standard complex Clifford algebra in dimension $n>0$, $A^0\cong\mathrm{Cl}_{0,n-1}(\mathbb C)$. Here an irreducible graded module means a nonzero graded module with no proper nonzero graded submodule ([[def-clifford-graded-algebra-module-and-tensor-product]]). Its isomorphism class, with parity-preserving maps, is exactly the class of a simple left $A^0$-module under the induction correspondence of [[thm-graded-module-classification-from-even-subalgebra]].

Consequently, if the applicable even-algebra entry in [[thm-real-complex-clifford-algebra-classification]] is $M_m(D)$, there is one irreducible graded module with even part the column module $D^m$; if it is $M_m(D)\oplus M_m(D)$, there are two, one supported on each factor. Their coefficient type is $D\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C,\mathbb H\}$. In complex scalars the type is always $\mathbb C$. At dimension zero, the algebra is purely even and has two irreducible graded modules, concentrated in parity $0$ and parity $1$, respectively.

For standard complex $\mathrm{Cl}_n(\mathbb C)$ with $n=2m>0$, the normalized volume element $\omega=i^m e_1\cdots e_n$ has square $1$, lies in the even subalgebra, and anticommutes with every odd generator. The two graded-module classes are the two choices of which $\omega$-eigenspace is placed in parity $0$; these are the two chiral parity conventions. For $n=2m+1$, the same formula gives an odd central element with square $1$; its two central idempotents are exchanged by the grading, so the two ungraded simple factors pair into the unique graded-simple class.

items.title: Low-signature real Clifford algebras as C, H, and matrix algebras
items.statement:
With $v^2=Q(v)1$ and signatures ordered $(+^p,-^q)$, the five signatures $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(2,0)$, $(1,1)$, and $(0,2)$ give respectively

$$
\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbb C,\qquad M_2(\mathbb R),\qquad M_2(\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbb H.
$$

This checks the sign and indexing conventions at the smallest dimensions.

items.title: Even-subalgebra types determine small graded Clifford modules
items.statement: For signatures $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(2,0)$, $(1,1)$, and $(0,2)$, the even subalgebras are respectively $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb C$, $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R$, and $\mathbb C$. Hence their graded-simple module counts and coefficient types are respectively one real, one real, one complex, two real, and one complex.
